description: REQ-201 through REQ-205 (and the Purity Boundary table / verification-architecture.md line 14) claim `~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/lib/child-spec.js::buildChildSpec` is 'reused UNMODIFIED' to assemble each new child's ledger row. It cannot be, as written. `buildChildSpec` throws `missing required field "childInbox"` (and `seedUsdc`, `constitutionHash`) for ANY of `undefined`, `null`, OR the empty string `''` (child-spec.js:26-30: `if (v === undefined || v === null || v === "") throw`). `childInbox` is an AgentMail email address in the OLD, pre-existing spawn design. The behavioral-spec.md itself explicitly declares that OLD design ('a 2026-06-16 DigitalOcean + AgentMail single-lineage design') architecturally superseded and out of scope, and verification-architecture.md line 31 states its AgentMail/DO provisioning code is 'NOT reused by any REQ in this spec'. Yet nowhere across REQ-201-205 does any requirement generate, assign, or even mention an AgentMail inbox for the child -- the new identity chain is EVM wallet (REQ-201) + optional Solana wallet (REQ-202) + $HOME isolation (REQ-203) + ERC-8004 register() (REQ-204) + mcp.json (REQ-205), with no email step at all. Confirmed by the function's own test suite (`__tests__/child-spec.test.js:62-67`, 'buildChildSpec requires every field') and by the function's actual production caller (`~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/run.sh:112-136`): when `AGENTMAIL_API_KEY` is unset, `run.sh` sets `CHILD_INBOX=""` (empty string) and still passes it straight into `buildChildSpec` -- which, per the function's own validation, throws on that empty string despite run.sh's own comment claiming the child is 'still born' in that case. As specified, an implementer literally cannot satisfy REQ-201-205's acceptance criteria ('reused for REQ-201-205's child record') without either (a) modifying buildChildSpec to make childInbox/seedUsdc optional -- directly violating the 'reused unmodified' constraint that is itself a binding acceptance criterion elsewhere in this spec (e.g. REQ-303's 'invoked with no source modification'), or (b) fabricating an AgentMail inbox nobody asked for and that contradicts the spec's own stated architecture, or (c) silently NOT calling buildChildSpec at all (in which case the spec's own claimed reuse is simply false and REQ-201's/verification-architecture's acceptance criteria referencing it are unverifiable as written).

additionalEvidence.note: test asserting buildChildSpec throws /missing/i when any field (including childInbox) is absent
production caller: CHILD_INBOX may be the empty string when AGENTMAIL_API_KEY is unset, yet is still passed into buildChildSpec unmodified
REQ-201 claims reuse of child-spec.js's distinct-wallet assertion for the new (non-AgentMail) flow; scope section declares AgentMail/DO provisioning superseded/out of scope
Purity Boundary Map claims child-spec.js reused unmodified for REQ-201-205, while separately stating the old AgentMail/DO code is not reused by any REQ
